intro.heading: SPY GEX levels
intro.description: See where SPY options exposure is concentrated. Start with the main put and call walls, then watch how price behaves around them.

chartDescription: Green bars show positive net gamma exposure. Coral bars show negative net gamma exposure. Taller bars mark larger concentrations.

readSteps.title: Find the nearby levels
readSteps.description: The put wall is the largest negative concentration. The call wall is the largest positive concentration in this expiry scope.

readSteps.title: Watch the price response
readSteps.description: Use these strikes as areas to monitor. A large bar alone does not tell you whether price will hold, break or reverse.

readSteps.title: Review the next condition
readSteps.description: In the full workspace, follow intraday walls and price reactions, then inspect an entry area, target and invalidation when a setup qualifies.

faqs.q: What does this free SPY page include?
faqs.a: One SPY end-of-day view with a fixed 2W expiry scope, the main positive and negative net GEX levels, and a strike chart. The displayed date identifies the actual EOD reading.

This page shows end-of-day exposure. Intraday wall tracking is part of the subscription and models changing price and time with a near-term 1W expiry scope. Intraday prices are delayed at least 15 minutes.

faqs.q: Do put and call walls predict where SPY will go?
faqs.a: A wall identifies a concentration of modeled exposure. It does not guarantee support, resistance or a price target. Watch the observed price response before treating a level as relevant to a trade.

faqs.q: Why can the levels differ from another view?
faqs.a: The included expirations, EOD date and view determine the calculation. This free view matches the dashboard with SPY, End of day, Latest EOD data and 2W selected. Next-session preparation excludes earlier expirations and may show different levels.
